articles.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams has moved on from 4-INT game, but frustration lingers
articles.description: Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Cubs outfielder was named NL MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズのQBカレブ・ウィリアムズ、4インターセプトの試合を乗り越えるも、悔しさは残る
articles.descriptionJa: カレブ・ウィリアムズはバイウィーク（試合のない週）を使い、不調のハムストリングを休ませるとともに、ナ・リーグMVPに選出された親友のカブス外野手ピート・クロウ＝アームストロングをサポートし、自身のキャリアで最悪の試合の一つを過去のものとした。
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Chicago Cubs outfielder was named National League MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.

The Chicago Bears went into their Week 10 bye with a 7-2 record after scraping by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 27-24 win. Williams found redemption after throwing a career-worst four interceptions against Tampa Bay by leading his first winning drive of the season to set up Cairo Santos for a 38-yard field goal as time expired.

Though the quarterback said he has moved past the interceptions, two of which he dubbed "funky" while calling another a "bad decision," the impact of his performance stayed with him during the time away.

"The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don't want to let my teammates down," Williams said. "That's always big for me. And in that situation, in those situations, I feel like I did. And so, that's the frustrating part that lingers."

Williams' four-interception performance was an aberration over his three-year career. Before the game against the Bucs, the quarterback had thrown four total interceptions over his previous 11 games dating to Nov. 28.

As the Bears gear up for the second half of their schedule, which features four NFC North games and meetings with AFC division leaders Jacksonville and Buffalo, the progress Williams has made earned high praise from coach Ben Johnson.

"He's playing fast right now," Johnson said. "He's got a great approach. He's doing a good job downloading the game plan. We don't feel like we're hindered in any way as a coaching staff from the schematics of what we're able to put in, the details, the alerts. He's just able to digest a lot more. He's seeing coverage really well with where his eyes should be tied into his feet also. So, we're really encouraged with where he's at. We just got to continue to push that envelope and see how far it will take us."

The Bears will need Williams at his best as they work through the league's toughest remaining schedule based on opponent win percentage. After entering its bye atop the NFC North, Chicago was in a three-way tie for first place in the division with Detroit and Minnesota by the end of Week 10.

It was a stark reminder of how quickly things can change in a tight division race. In one week, the Bears went from No. 2 to No. 6 in the NFC playoff bracket.

Chicago hosts New Orleans (3-6) on Sunday before turning around for a trip to Detroit on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears have yet to win a division game after early losses to the Vikings and Green Bay.

"The pressure idea ... I don't think we have that here inside the building," Williams said. "I think that's the biggest thing is us understanding it only matters what we think, what we feel. You know one week we can be Super Bowl contenders, one week we can be playoff contenders,

articles.headline: Trail Blazers rule star Deni Avdija out vs. Timberwolves with sore foot
articles.description: The Trail Blazers ruled out star Deni Avdija for Tuesday night's game against the Timberwolves due to a sore left foot.
articles.headlineJa: トレイルブレイザーズ、足の痛みによりティンバーウルブズ戦にデニ・アブディヤが出場せず
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズは、左足の痛みのため、火曜夜のティンバーウルブズ戦にスター選手のデニ・アブディヤが出場しないことを発表した。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Portland Trail Blazers star Deni Avdija will miss Tuesday's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves with a sore left foot.

Avdija was listed as questionable on the injury report but attempted to warm up on the court before being ruled out.

Avdija scored 27 points on 11 of 19 shooting with eight rebounds and four assists in Portland's 106-98 loss on Monday night in Minnesota. This will be his first missed game of the season.

Portland is also missing Ja Morant (left hamstring) and Shaedon Sharpe (right meniscus).

articles.headline: Terry Rozier co-defendant signals intent to change plea in NBA betting case
articles.description: Deniro Laster, a co-defendant in the federal sports betting case involving NBA player Terry Rozier, has signaled his intent to plead guilty.
articles.headlineJa: NBA賭博事件、テリー・ロジアーの共同被告が認否の変更を示唆
articles.descriptionJa: NBA選手のテリー・ロジアーが関与した連邦スポーツ賭博事件の共同被告であるデニロ・ラスターが、有罪を認める意向を示した。
articles.body:
A key co-defendant in the federal sports betting case involving NBA player Terry Rozier signaled his intent to change his plea, according to a docket entry in the case Tuesday.

Deniro Laster, who allegedly collaborated with Rozier in the fraudulent betting scheme, initially pleaded not guilty and was scheduled to stand trial alongside the NBA player on Feb. 8 in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. Instead, Laster will appear before a federal magistrate on Dec. 2 to change his plea.

It is not immediately clear whether Laster is changing his plea as part of an agreement with prosecutors or, if so, whether such an agreement would require him to participate in the government's case against Rozier.

Attorneys for Laster and Rozier did not immediately reply to messages from ESPN on Tuesday afternoon. A spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York declined to comment.

The intent to change the plea casts an even brighter spotlight on the relationship between Laster and Rozier, childhood friends whom prosecutors say worked hand in hand to enable a web of alleged fixers to place fraudulent bets.

Specifically, the government alleges Rozier told Laster that he planned to leave a March 2023 game between the Charlotte Hornets and the New Orleans Pelicans early, and that Laster sold that information to fellow sports bettors so they could place fraudulent bets on Rozier's performance. In exchange for the information, Rozier allegedly negotiated a bribe of roughly $100,000, which he agreed to share with Laster.

Rozier's attorneys have since argued in court records that Laster acted without their client's knowledge, citing a text message sent by Laster to an unidentified recipient saying, "Dont tell chum bout the bet." They say "Chum" is Rozier's nickname.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, have said they have evidence suggesting that text message exchange "does not relate to sports gambling." And they also have said that Rozier has spent "hundreds of thousands of dollars" bankrolling Laster's legal defense and questioned why Rozier would do so if Laster, as Rozier has contended, sold information about the NBA player behind his back.

"Rozier's defense is that Laster acted independently and without Rozier's knowledge," prosecutors wrote in a filing last week. "Yet Rozier continues to pay Laster's legal fees. They continued to communicate, post-indictment, in violation of their bond conditions. That makes little sense if Laster betrayed him. It is instead consistent with a conspiratorial relationship that continues to this day."

Rozier's attorney, David Markus, wrote in his own filing last week that Rozier is innocent and "unlike every other individual charged in this sweeping conspiracy, he never placed a bet on an NBA game or player prop."

articles.headline: 76ers' LeBron James sues makers of AI sports-betting app 'Bron'
articles.description: NBA superstar LeBron James sued the makers of an AI sports-betting app Tuesday, saying they have deliberately violated his publicity rights and trademarks by calling it "Bron" and using artificially generated images of him in their marketing.
articles.headlineJa: 76ersのレブロン・ジェームズ、AIスポーツ賭博アプリ「Bron」の開発者を提訴
articles.descriptionJa: NBAのスーパースター、レブロン・ジェームズは火曜日、AIスポーツ賭博アプリの開発者を提訴した。アプリに「Bron」という名称を付け、マーケティングに彼のAI生成画像を使用したことで、パブリシティ権と商標権を意図的に侵害したと主張している。
articles.body:
NBA superstar LeBron James sued the makers of an AI sports-betting app Tuesday, saying they have deliberately violated his publicity rights and trademarks by calling it "Bron" and using artificially generated images of him in their marketing.

In a lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in New York, James' attorneys called it "a willful, bad-faith tactic" to use the player's fame, likeness and nickname to promote "a new and unknown product."

The complaint asks the court to block the makers from using the Philadelphia 76ers star's name, to give up any money they've already made and to award damages -- including fair market value for the use of his name as well as punitive damages.

"Defendants did not care that they had engaged in illegal conduct to gain notoriety for their previously unknown app," the lawsuit states. "They intentionally created the false impression that Mr. James endorsed and was affiliated with their Bron App, in an effort to drive downloads and paid subscriptions."

Messages sent by The Associated Press through the app's website and to email addresses for its founders seeking comment were not immediately returned Tuesday.

The app's developer, PlayVision Inc., is based in California. It was launched by chief executive Anish Gupta and chief technology officer Marc Zoghby in 2025, with backing from the startup accelerator Y Combinator, as a program that would use artificial intelligence to analyze game and practice footage for sports teams and fans.

This year, the company released its "Bron" app, which it says does not take direct wagers but charges a subscription fee for services such as bet tracking and odds comparisons. It launched a marketing campaign this month that featured an image of a person resembling James -- down to his tattoos, voice and No. 23 jersey -- sitting in a locker room and scrolling through the app.

James' lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter, as previously reported by Front Office Sports. The company took the ad down, but not before it had been reposted and viewed about 1 million times, the lawsuit said.

Gupta responded to the attorneys' demand on social media by writing that the app would get a new name, but no new name had been adopted by the time the lawsuit was filed, leading James' legal team to suggest the company was milking the controversy for attention. Gupta wrote on social media this week that the new name will be announced Wednesday.

The lawsuit notes that James typically commands tens of millions of dollars for such endorsement deals and that he already has an exclusive deal with the prediction market platform Polymarket. It alleges that the app's marketing was especially harmful in part because it showed the AI-generated James scrolling through bets involving NBA players.

articles.headline: Miami Heat unveil 'A Night in Vice City' court, activities ahead of GTA VI release
articles.description: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date Thursday, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ヒート、GTA VI発売を前に「A Night in Vice City」コートとイベントを公開
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜日に待望の『グランド・セフト・オート VI』の発売を控え、ヒートはロックスター・ゲームズと提携し、前夜に話題のリードアップイベントを開催する。
articles.body:
The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now, but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Wednesday will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center.

With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Thursday, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.

Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings, including before and during the game.

Fans are encouraged to arrive early with with the team's "Vice City" collection available starting two hours before tipoff. There will be GTA VI-inspired cars set outside Kaseya Center on the West Plaza plus a GTA IV logo next to the rides for pictures. Similar spots for photos will be scattered throughout the arena and East Plaza. Official music from the game is going to be played in-arena, while Cluckin' Bell and Burger Joint -- two fast food restaurants from the GTA series -- will be at select concessions in Kaseya Center.

The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms. Even the roof of Kaseya Center is going to be altered to read: "Welcome to Vice City." 

Miami revealed the pink, white and blue hardwood court Tuesday, featuring "Vice City" in the center and "I heart Vice City" on a baseline. The "VI" logo also appears near the dunker spot on each side of the court.

The jerseys, unveiled on Nov. 6., build on the team's past "Vice" alternates with nods to Grand Theft Auto VI and Travis Scott's Cactus Jack brand. The black Swingman jersey features pink and white accents, "Vice City" across the chest, Scott's signature flipped Nike Swoosh and a "VI" nod to the game. Six pink stars and Cactus Jack branding appear at the hem alongside a tag featuring Rockstar Games, the Heat and Cactus Jack.

Both the on-court and Swingman versions will be available in limited quantities Wednesday.

According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience."

The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event on Nov. 5., lighting up the "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of its arena. Players have expressed excitement, including Giannis Antetokounmpo and Klay Thompson, an avid gamer.

"I understand the hype and feel like a lot of people in this locker room have played the game. They're excited for the game to come out," Antetokounmpo said Monday. "Just be able to be part of one of the most talked about video games. It's fun. I heard that we have special jerseys and special court, so I'm excited for that, excited for the energy."

Antetokounmpo added that the main thing for the Heat though is that they come out and win.

articles.headline: 76ers' Jaylen Brown (hamstring) to miss Wednesday's game vs. Magic
articles.description: Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown will miss Wednesday's game against the Orlando Magic with a left hamstring strain, the Sixers announced Tuesday afternoon.
articles.headlineJa: 76ersのジェイレン・ブラウン（ハムストリング）、水曜のマジック戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: フィラデルフィア・76ersのフォワード、ジェイレン・ブラウンは、左ハムストリングの肉離れのため水曜日のオーランド・マジック戦を欠場すると、チームが火曜午後に発表した。
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown will miss Wednesday's road game against the Orlando Magic with a left hamstring strain, the team said Tuesday.

Brown will be reevaluated ahead of Saturday's home matchup against the Milwaukee Bucks, a source told ESPN.

LeBron James, who missed the Sixers' 135-123 win over the Nets on Monday with low back management, has no injury designation for the Magic game. 

Brown exited late in the fourth quarter of Monday's win with the hamstring strain. It was one of two injuries he suffered in the game, in which he tied his season-high of 31 points and added 13 rebounds. In the first quarter he bumped heads with forward Julius Randle and was left bleeding on the court, in a tense moment that saw both benches circle around him.

Wednesday night will be the second game Brown has missed this season. His only other absence was the Sixers' NBA Cup victory over the New York Knicks on Oct. 30, where he sat out with left knee soreness.

Brown has found his stride in recent weeks, with back-to-back 31-point games in the Sixers' past two wins. He is averaging 24.6 points this month, 4.8 more than October; his field goal percentage in November is 53.7%, up from 43.6% last month.

"I'm feeling a little bit more comfortable ... starting to feel a little bit more at home," Brown said Monday night.

Big men Adem Bona (neck) and Dominick Barlow (back) are also out against the Magic. Barlow hasn't played yet this season.

articles.headline: Raptors say Kawhi Leonard progressing but out at least another week
articles.description: The Raptors said Tuesday that while Kawhi Leonard is progressing in his recovery from left knee swelling, he will remain out for at least another week.
articles.headlineJa: ラプターズ、カワイ・レナードの回復は進むも、少なくともあと1週間は欠場
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズは火曜日、カワイ・レナードの左膝の腫れの回復は進んでいるものの、少なくともあと1週間は欠場が続く見込みであることを明らかにした。
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors said Tuesday that while Kawhi Leonard is progressing in his recovery from left knee swelling, he will remain out for at least another week.

Leonard, who has been sidelined since Oct. 23, "has progressed in his strength and conditioning program," and another update will be provided in a week, the team said.

The seven-time All-Star will miss four more games before the next scheduled update; he has already missed 11 games this season while appearing in just two in his first campaign back with the Raptors.

Leonard, 35, had an MRI on his knee last month that showed no structural damage. He previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL.

Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in his two games played in his second stint with Toronto. He was traded to the Raptors from the LA Clippers this offseason following a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons in Los Angeles.

He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

articles.headline: Arrest warrants issued for robbery of Steelers' Max Iheanachor
articles.description: Arrest warrants have been issued for three individuals in connection with the burglary of the home of Steelers first-round pick Max Iheanachor, police said.
articles.headlineJa: スチールのマックス・イエアナチョルの強盗事件で逮捕状が発行
articles.descriptionJa: 警察によると、スチールのドラフト1巡目指名選手マックス・イエアナチョルの自宅への強盗事件に関連して、3名に対して逮捕状が発行された。
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Arrest warrants have been issued for three individuals in connection with the burglary of the home of Steelers first-round pick Max Iheanachor, the Pittsburgh police department announced Tuesday.

Los Angeles residents Winter Brantley, 25, Andre Castle Jr., 23, and Lamar Stewart, 45, allegedly broke into Iheanachor's home in late August. Each faces multiple charges of burglary, criminal trespass, theft by unlawful taking, receiving stolen property and conspiracy, according to the police. According to the criminal complaint, Brantley is the sister of Iheanachor's roommate.

Pittsburgh detectives are working with the U.S. Marshals Service in California to take the three into custody.

More than $200,000 worth of jewelry and designer items were taken from Iheanachor's home in the Mount Washington neighborhood of Pittsburgh, police said in the release. Iheanachor was in New York for the Steelers' preseason finale against the Bills when the robbery occurred.

Iheanachor's roommate, Ashley Brantley, told police in an October interview that he had been "beefing" with his sister on and off over the past year, according to the complaint. Detectives zeroed in on the trio with the help of security cameras in the neighborhood that spotted a dark Audi SUV at Iheanachor's residence on the day of the break-in, receipts for the credit card used to book the rental car used in the burglary and security footage at the Pittsburgh airport, per the complaint.

Police added that the investigation is ongoing.

Iheanachor, an Arizona State product selected with the 21st pick earlier this year, has started the Steelers' past seven games at right tackle.

articles.headline: Source: Jordan Phillips latest Dolphins DT to suffer season-ending injury
articles.description: Dolphins DT Jordan Phillips will miss the rest of the season with torn biceps, a source confirmed to ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：ドルフィンズのジョーダン・フィリップス、今季絶望の負傷
articles.descriptionJa: ドルフィンズのDTジョーダン・フィリップスは上腕二頭筋の断裂により今季残り全試合を欠場することになる、と情報筋がESPNに明かした。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Dolphins defensive tackle Jordan Phillips will miss the rest of the season with torn biceps, a source confirmed Tuesday to ESPN, adding to a string of season-ending injuries Miami has suffered over the past two weeks.

Phillips left Sunday's loss to the Colts in the fourth quarter and did not return. Additional testing this week confirmed his diagnosis, and the team placed Phillips on injured reserve Tuesday.

He is Miami's third defensive tackle to land on season-ending IR in the past two weeks, joining Zach Sieler and Zeek Biggers.

The Dolphins' defensive tackle room is now the thinnest on its team, led by former first-round draft pick Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper Jr., who was signed from the practice squad last week. Miami also signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson to the active roster from the practice squad and added defensive lineman Matthew Butler to the practice squad.

Grant and Cooper finished the game on the field for Miami against the Colts, who completed the quarter with 30 total yards in 13 plays.

"They battled," coach Jeff Hafley said Monday. "In the fourth quarter, I think we had them go three-and-out two or three times to get the ball back to the offense. I give those guys a lot of credit, but it's hard when you're down to two guys there at the end of the game. It's hard with three because those guys rotate so much, taking on the double-teams and all the strain and the effort, so that was tough sledding against a good back yesterday."

The Dolphins selected Phillips in the fifth round in 2025, and he quickly established himself as a rotational defensive lineman, playing 43.4% of their defensive snaps as a rookie. He took on a larger role this season and had played 60% of the team's snaps through nine games.

Phillips, 22, is considered a key part of the NFL's youngest defense, which ranks 10th in yards allowed per game this season. After Sieler's injury in Week 9, Hafley mentioned Phillips as one of the players he expected to step up and lead Miami's defensive line room.

"The way he plays, the way he goes about everything in this building," Hafley said. "I mean, he is a great example of leadership, and whether or not he's a second-year player only, it's going to be his time now to help out those other players."

Beyond the trio of defensive tackles, the Dolphins placed quarterback Malik Willis on IR last week with a groin injury that Hafley said spread to his core. The team is hopeful Willis returns after missing a mandated minimum four games. Hafley said Monday that no surgery is planned for Willis at this time but that the decision is not final.

In other moves Tuesday, the Dolphins signed quarterback Brady Cook and edge rusher Eric Watts to the active roster off the practice squad. Cook will back up interim starter Kyle McCord.

Miami also added several players to the practice squad, including receiver Brady Boyd, defensive linemen Chris Smith and Matthew Butler and kicker Daniel Carlson.

articles.headline: JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears
articles.description: JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.
articles.body:
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.

The 16-year-old asked to leave United in September and sources told ESPN that he is on the brink of a move to Real Madrid. He had been training in Madrid earlier this month.

"Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams," he said in the video on Instagram.

"Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I'll always treasure.

"To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ."

- Man United's JJ Gabriel amid Real Madrid move talk: 'Dream to win a Ballon d'Or'

- Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at height of Man United career

United will consider legal action if they believe illegal approaches were made while Gabriel was under contract at Old Trafford, sources said.

Gabriel's Irish passport, which allows him to join any club in the European Union, could help facilitate the transfer under FIFA regulations governing international moves for players aged between 16 and 18, with January the first opportunity for him to be registered.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: AC Milan, Juventus eye USMNT's Folarin Balogun
articles.description: AS Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun is reportedly linked to two of Italy's biggest clubs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw is on the radar of Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus ahead of the January transfer window, Calciomercato has reported. The USMNT striker's agent Jorge Mendes has contacted both clubs, who are looking to strengthen their attacking options, after a €40 million move to Everton collapsed at the end of the last window. The 25-year-old, who is under contract at Monaco until June 2028, is reportedly open to the idea of playing in Serie A.

- Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies' backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.

- Real Madrid are weighing up a move to bring Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Chema Andrés back to the club, as per TEAMtalk. Chema, 21, came through the Madrid youth team ranks but left in 2025 and has impressed since arriving at VfB Stuttgart in the summer. However, a deal could be complicated as there is uncertainty over his contractual situation, with Brighton previously disputing suggestions that Madrid retain an option to re-sign him permanently. Madrid also monitoring highly-rated Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for £46 million this summer.

- Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City's financial charges.

- Bayern Munich youth goalkeeper Leonard Prescott could leave  on a free transfer next summer, after contract talks stalled, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Brighton and Aston Villa are among the clubs tracking his development, says Sky Germany. Prescott, 17, was born in New York but has represented Germany at U17 and is very highly rated.

articles.headline: Matheus Nunes in talks to extend Man City deal - sources
articles.description: Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.

Nunes has a deal until 2028, but City are keen to agree fresh terms. Negotiations are ongoing, although sources have told ESPN that talks are not yet at an advanced stage.

The Portugal international is closing in on 150 appearances for the club after arriving from Wolves in 2023. Initially joining as a midfielder, he was converted to a full-back under former boss Pep Guardiola.

Nunes appeared in 34 of City's 38 Premier League games last season with his form convincing club bosses to strengthen other areas of the squad over the summer instead of at right-back.

Meanwhile, City are facing a decision about whether to keep midfielder Mateo Kovacic. The Croatian is out of contract at the end of the season and can negotiate with clubs outside the Premier League from January.

Kovacic has struggled for game time so far this season and has made just one Premier League start under new manager Enzo Maresca.

articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールは、ついに夏の移籍騒動を乗り越えたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: 夏の移籍を巡る不透明な状況とシーズン序盤の不調を経て、ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールはレアル・マドリードとブラジル代表で復活への道を歩んでいる。
articles.body:
Vinícius Júnior has earned hundreds of millions of euros thanks to his feet. Thunderous goals off his instep, intuitive, imaginative crosses bending in from his outstep, defender-fooling step-overs while full-tilt sprinting at 35kmh. The Real Madrid and Brazil star is a winger who's often been a few steps ahead of opponents.

But the metaphorical "first step" that the 26-year-old took in Singapore on Monday -- starting to solve a problem by admitting that there has been one -- might be the best foot forward he's taken in many months.

You've probably consumed his words by now -- with the same hunger as he appears to have consumed summer treats that the regular Joe is allowed but are next to prohibited for elite athletes. Most especially if, simultaneously, they are skimping on the high-intensity, calorie-burning exercise which is now the regimented, obligatory companion of any top footballer during the brief summer weeks when they're not training and playing.

"I don't think I prepared myself well enough for the new season," Vinícius said. "I took advantage of the holidays to rest, to disconnect from soccer and to spend more family time. The final result was that I trained less than in previous summers."

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- As Nike replaces Adidas, is Champions League star ball on its way out?

- 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!

Maybe Vinícius received a timely call from Eden Hazard, the last star to arrive back for a Real Madrid preseason carrying much more weight than is permissible? I'm being fanciful, but wouldn't it be nice to think that one ex-magician might be looking out for a current wing-wizard? Because the Belgian, who still lives in Madrid and remains under the romantic spell of the greatest club in the world (I know because he told me so), is a good morality tale for his Brazilian successor.

"I wouldn't say I was overdoing what I ate -- I just wasn't paying attention," Hazard admitted to L'Equipe soon after he retired from football in 2023, relinquishing a full year of a multi-million contract with Madrid. "I didn't attach any importance to it. I'm a bon vivant; I enjoy eating with friends, having a drink. Dieting sucks -- it's useless ... well, I suppose it's fine if you want to keep playing until you're 40.

"That summer when I arrived at Madrid, I had just finished an incredible season with Chelsea. I told myself, 'Now that I'm at Real, this might be one of the last vacations where I can ... so, I just let myself go."

It cost Hazard acceleration, sharpness of those quick feet of his, injury avoidance, injury recuperation, the faith of his coach, the fans and the media. Reading those words, do you recognise the comparisons with much of Vinícius' season thus far?

Now, Vinícius is a universe away from what became Hazard's extreme situation. But the Brazilian is currently in direct competition for his place on Madrid's left wing with €125 mil
